summary: Checked every factual statement in gtd-script.txt (22 segments, 49 rows) against the originals, not just the ledger. R = <scratchpad>/research; V = vault/snapshots/local. Tally: 37 supported, 10 overreach, 1 wrong, 1 unsupported. Fix before shipping: (1) b4 says the two objectives are in the 第一版 引言; they are at the opening of chapter 1 (excerpt L113), and the ledger's reviewer had already flagged the mislabel. (2) b3 says Allen said only wording changed; he also said he updated a bunch of stuff, added new cognition research, and addressed a broader audience. The rename of the five steps is also dated loosely: the new labels were on the company site by 2014-05-31, before the March 2015 book, and the 2015 body text was never read. (3) b15 adds 人也就不再信它, which is not in the Ferriss passage; EP17 L87-91 runs the other way. (4) b14 puts a company checklist and Ferriss's 'an hour or two' under one 'Allen 说'. (5) b18 says no research is cited; the staff comment relaying Allen says the 2015 edition adds cognition research (unread), and the 2001 excerpt contains third-party praise blurbs and a client testimonial, so 只有他本人的叙述 should read 没有独立研究. (6) b21 says nobody but Saraf has spoken about how Palantir used the book; Qureshi (L46) says new hires were sent a copy, and the series itself relies on that. (7) Smaller items: b2 就是在这种处境里 is an adjacency inference; b7 难的是第二个目标 is an unlabelled narrator inference; b16 attaches the one-hour-a-day figure to the coached mid-to-senior professionals, but the handout says typical professional; b19 代价 is an unlabelled narrator framing, whereas Saraf calls the visibility the best part. The only narrator reading explicitly labelled (b21 我的读法 / 这是推论) is labelled correctly. The ledger entries gtd.disorganization-definition and gtd.about-2015-edition (both needs-fix) are not used in this script, so those errors do not carry over.

rows.statement: The previous episode was about reading status in a room (Impro).
rows.source_locator: scratchpad/review/im-script.txt im.b3-b19 (status) and im.o1 (names Getting Things Done as next); scratchpad/review/pr-script.txt pr.i1 follows this episode.
rows.note: Series order is consistent: Impro, then GTD, then the Dalio PDF.

rows.statement: A person holds dozens to a hundred-plus things at once.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/e27.txt L34-37 (about 150-220 next actions, 30-100 projects); R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L181 ('between 30 and a hundred' projects).
rows.note: Framing only. The numbers are Allen's own estimates for the mid-to-senior professionals he coaches.

rows.statement: Sanjay Saraf joined Palantir in 2015.
rows.source_locator: R/overview/data/saraf.clean.txt L12 ('When I joined Palantir in 2015').

rows.statement: He recalls that every outgoing email had to be BCC'd to a mailing list of the whole team.
rows.source_locator: R/overview/data/saraf.clean.txt L56 ('All email communication with the outside world had to BCC a mailing list with everyone on the team').
rows.note: The source is undated past tense. '那时' ties it to 2015 slightly more tightly than the post does.

rows.statement: Important client meetings required a written meeting report sent to a long list of people.
rows.source_locator: R/overview/data/saraf.clean.txt L56 ('meeting report ... mailing list that had a very wide distribution - often the entire company').
rows.note: '一长串人' understates 'often the entire company'. 纪要 for 'meeting report' is acceptable.

rows.statement: As a result you either drowned in email or learned to set up filters.
rows.source_locator: R/overview/data/saraf.clean.txt L57 ('you faced two options: 1) drown in your email or 2) get good at setting up email filters and clearing your inbox').
rows.note: Source says two options, not two outcomes. The script's '结果' is a mild shift and drops 'clearing your inbox'.

rows.statement: Saraf says Getting Things Done first became a commonly recommended book and later required reading for new hires.
rows.source_locator: R/overview/data/saraf.clean.txt L57 ('became a commonly recommended book and eventually became part of the mandated reading for new hires').
rows.note: Attributed to Saraf correctly. 'Part of the mandated reading' is slightly softer than 必读.

rows.statement: '就是在这种处境里': the book became recommended and then required in exactly this email-flood situation.
rows.source_locator: R/overview/data/saraf.clean.txt L57: the GTD sentence directly follows the two-options sentence in the same paragraph.
rows.note: Saraf places the sentences next to each other but does not say GTD arose because of, or in, the email flood. The causal or situational link is the script's own, not stated by the source.

rows.statement: The only text the narrator could read is the publisher's excerpt of the first edition, ending at the start of chapter 1; the rest relies on Allen's website, handouts and interviews.
rows.source_locator: V/palantir-20261006/allen-gtd-official-excerpt.txt L68-71 (copyright page: Viking 2001, Penguin 2003) and L143 (ends at the heading 'The Old Models and Habits Are Insufficient'); V/palantir-20261006/README.md.
rows.note: The edition identity rests on the copyright page. The excerpt text sits on the PRH page registered for the 2015 edition (ISBN 9780143126560). The 2001 wording ('twenty-plus years') is consistent with a 2001 text.

rows.statement: The author is David Allen and the first edition came out in 2001.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/raw/about.txt L71-72 ('2001 ... The first edition'); excerpt L68-71.

rows.statement: A fully rewritten second edition came out in 2015.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/raw/about.txt L53-54 ('Second edition ... Completely rewritten'); R/execution-system/posts/p01.txt L19 and L31 (interviewer calls it 'second edition').
rows.note: 'Second edition' is the company's own label (also the interviewer's); Penguin calls it the revised edition. The script correctly does not say '同时 25 种语言'.

rows.statement: The five steps got different names in the new edition.
rows.source_locator: Old names: excerpt L12-16 (chapter titles Collection / Processing / Organizing / Reviewing / Doing); R/execution-system/posts/2012_05_5-phases-of-gtd-workflow.txt L29 (Collect, Process, Organize, Review & Do). New names: R/execution-system/wayback/fs_20140531143950.html with img/02_Clarify_Caption.png and 04_Reflect_Caption.png; R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L306-307. Wording change: R/execution-system/posts/2015_03_getting-things-done-updated-for-2015.txt L45.
rows.note: The renaming itself is documented, but only across four separate materials. The Capture/Clarify/Organize/Reflect/Engage labels were on the company site by 2014-05-31, ten months before the March 2015 book. The 2015 body text was never read; the ledger says so in gtd.version-split. Allen says only 'subtle changes in the vocabulary and descriptions of the components'. Tying the rename to the 2015 edition is inferred, not stated.

rows.statement: Allen says the principles did not change at all.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/p01.txt L32 ('No, the principles haven't changed at all'); R/execution-system/posts/2015_03_getting-things-done-updated-for-2015.txt L45 ('The GTD methodology hasn't changed').
rows.note: The L45 statement is a staff comment relaying Allen, dated 2018-01-29.

rows.statement: What changed was only the wording ('改的是措辞').
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/2015_03_getting-things-done-updated-for-2015.txt L45 (broader audience, vocabulary changes, 'added new research from the field of cognition'); R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L373 ('I've updated a bunch of stuff and tweaked the language-ing a good bit'); V/palantir-20261006/allen-gtd-publisher-page.html.txt (publisher copy: rewritten start to finish, new tools and technologies).
rows.note: Allen says the principles did not change, but he also says he updated content, added cognition research and wrote for a broader audience. Wording was one of several changes, not the only one.

rows.statement: In the first edition's introduction (引言) he reduces the method to two objectives.
rows.source_locator: V/palantir-20261006/allen-gtd-official-excerpt.txt L113 (chapter 1 'A New Practice for a New Reality', first lines after the Kekich epigraph). The introduction ('Welcome to Getting Things Done', L84-103) does not contain the two objectives.
rows.note: Content is right; the locator is wrong. The ledger reviewer already said to change 引言 to 第 1 章开头, and the script kept the mislabel.

rows.statement: Goal 1: get everything to be done (now, later, someday; big, small) into a trusted system outside the head.
rows.source_locator: excerpt L113 ('capturing all the things that need to get done—now, later, someday, big, little, or in between—into a logical and trusted system outside of your head and off your mind').
rows.note: Drops 'logical' and 'or in between'; harmless.

rows.statement: Goal 2: make a decision in advance about everything you let into your life.
rows.source_locator: excerpt L113 ('disciplining yourself to make front-end decisions about all of the "inputs" you let into your life').
rows.note: The ledger also says to keep the 'next actions you can implement or renegotiate' clause; the script leaves it out, which is fine.

rows.statement: Allen says the part of the brain that holds commitments has no sense of past or future, thinks you should buy cat food 24 hours a day, and so wakes you at 3 a.m.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L119 (Tim Ferriss Show #384, 2019); also R/execution-system/posts/e35.txt ('no sense of past or future').
rows.note: Close paraphrase. The script does not name the interview, which is fine.

rows.statement: Allen says most people use their head as an office, but the head is a very bad office.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L98 ('your head's a crappy office. And most people are still using their head as their office').

rows.statement: Allen says anyone who keeps a calendar already does this: put what you cannot remember into a system and build the habit of looking at it at the right time.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/p01.txt L32 ('Anybody who keeps a calendar is already doing that ... a behavior that trusts you're going to look at that at the right time').

rows.statement: The hard one is the second objective.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L182-188 ('People avoid that decision like the plague'; L183 'It's not hard'; L188 'Thinking's hard').
rows.note: Allen does not rank the two objectives by difficulty. In the same passage he says both 'It's not hard' and 'Thinking's hard'. This is the narrator's own inference and is not labelled as such.

rows.statement: Allen cites Drucker: a knowledge worker's biggest task is defining their own work because work is not self-evident, and an incoming email does not tell you what to do with it.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/e27.txt L15 ('your biggest task is defining what your work is ... your work is not self-evident. The e-mail ... does not tell you what to do about that e-mail').
rows.note: It is Allen's paraphrase of Drucker ('he would caution all of you'), and the script frames it as 'Allen 引过'. Correct.

rows.statement: For each item Allen has people ask what it is and whether it needs action. Non-actionable items have only three destinations: trash, reference, or incubate (decide later).
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/e27.txt L15-25 ('three subcategories of non-actionable things': trash, reference material, incubate); R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L190 ('reference or trash or incubate').
rows.note: '只有' is Allen's 'basically'. Fine.

rows.statement: For actionable items, define the next action: the next visible, concrete action if you had nothing else to do but this.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/e27.txt L25 ('the next physical, visible action you would need to take, if you had nothing else to do in your life but finish [it]').

rows.statement: Anything one action cannot finish is logged as a project, with the desired outcome stated.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/e27.txt L36 ('anything you can't finish with one action step ... What's the outcome?').

rows.statement: Allen's example: the word 'Mom' on a list is a mere reminder; rewritten, the project is a birthday party for mom and the next step is calling the sister to ask what to do.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/2011_02_how-is-a-next-action-list-different-from-a-to-do-list.txt L30; R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L185.
rows.note: Source says 'Mom' is an 'unclarified to do item' and 'vague', not a 'reminder'. This is a minor paraphrase. The project and next-action wording matches both versions.

rows.statement: Allen says more than 90% of the to-do lists he has seen are made of unclear items.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/2011_02_how-is-a-next-action-list-different-from-a-to-do-list.txt L30 ('90+ % of the to do lists I've seen are incomplete inventories of still-unclear things').
rows.note: The figure is Allen's impression with no sample. '他见过的' hedges it adequately. It is about lists, not 90% of items.

rows.statement: A list still feels oppressive because the necessary thinking has not been finished.
rows.source_locator: Same post L30 ('actually finishes the thinking ... Because "Mom" is vague, it still triggers stress'); R/execution-system/posts/e27.txt L27 ('You haven't finished your thinking about it').
rows.note: Allen's own causal claim, attributed to him ('他说').

rows.statement: Two-minute rule: once the next action is set, if you need to do it anyway and it takes under two minutes, do it on the spot; the reason is purely efficiency, since looking at it again later takes longer than doing it.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/2020_05_the-two-minute-rule-2.txt L44-45 ('pure efficiency factor'; 'if you need to do it at all'); R/execution-system/posts/e27.txt L29 ('once you determine a next action, if you're ever gonna do it at all ... it would take you longer to track it and look at it again').
rows.note: Both conditions (next action determined; you need to do it at all) are stated by Allen. Correctly framed.

rows.statement: Allen also says it is not a hard rule; you can decide at any time to do something longer.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/2011_06_when-to-use-gtds-two-minute-rule.txt L30 ('At any time you can decide to do something that takes more than two minutes ... No hard fast rules').
rows.note: Said in the context of processing an email inbox.

rows.statement: Joe Lonsdale's piece on Peter Thiel mentions it in a single sentence: in GTD you don't put off tasks that take only a few minutes.
rows.source_locator: V/palantir-20261006/lonsdale-lessons-from-peter-thiel.html.txt (lesson 6, char offset about 45781, line 480); R/overview/data/lonsdale.clean.txt L57 ('Similarly, in GTD, you don't put off tasks that only take a couple minutes').
rows.note: It is the only GTD mention in the article. Two small hedges: Lonsdale wrote 'a couple minutes' (script says 几分钟). Authorship by Lonsdale rests on the byline card; the page's intro is third person ('These lessons summarize what Joe Lonsdale learned...'). Page date 2010-04-11 is metadata.

rows.statement: Lonsdale dropped the two preceding conditions.
rows.source_locator: Lonsdale L57 versus R/execution-system/posts/2020_05_the-two-minute-rule-2.txt L44-45 and e27.txt L29.
rows.note: Correct: his sentence carries no 'next action already decided' and no 'you were going to do it anyway', and no 'not a hard rule'.

rows.statement: Allen's full practice is an hour or two each week.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L307 ('take an hour or two, at least once a week'); L314 ('usually about every seven days').
rows.note: Spoken by Allen. Note 'at least once a week'.

rows.statement: 'Allen 说' the full practice is to empty every inbox, go through the lists, and check each project has at least one current next action.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/pdfs/GTD-WeeklyReview.txt L11-15 and L31-34 (company checklist, © David Allen Company, dated 20MAY2015); R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L307.
rows.note: Substance is right, but the detailed steps come from the company's Weekly Review sheet, which gives no time estimate. 'An hour or two' is from the Ferriss interview. Two sources are spliced under 'Allen 说'.

rows.statement: Without the weekly review the system soon goes out of date and people drop the whole method.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L314 ('If you don't do that, it gets out of date. You'll fall off the wagon pretty fast').

rows.statement: '人也就不再信它': people then stop trusting the system.
rows.source_locator: Not in R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L314. Nearest: R/execution-system/posts/2016_06_ten-common-questions-about-gtd.txt L87-91.
rows.note: This inserts a trust step that the Ferriss passage does not state. EP17 L87-91 runs the opposite direction: if you still trust your mind rather than the system, you won't be motivated to do the review. Replace with the source's 'fall off the wagon'.

rows.statement: For mid-to-senior executives Allen coaches, getting everything that holds their attention out takes one to six hours.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L113 ('for the mid- to senior level professional that we actually coach ... one to six hours, just to capture what has their attention'); also L182.
rows.note: '头一回' is a mild gloss; the context is the first thing done in a coaching session.

rows.statement: Day to day, handling new input costs those same people an average of an hour a day.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/pdfs/Threefold-Nature-of-Work.txt L68-70 ('requires an average of one hour per day, for the typical professional ... just to stay current').
rows.note: The handout says the typical professional, not the coached mid-to-senior executives. The script attaches the figure to the population from the previous sentence.

rows.statement: Allen says it is not an overnight trick but a craft you practise for a lifetime.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/2015_09_gtd-is-not-an-overnight-little-time-management-tip.txt L29 (signed '-David Allen').

rows.statement: It does not make problems disappear; it clarifies them so they can be negotiated.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/posts/2016_06_ten-common-questions-about-gtd.txt L53 (speaker DAVID ALLEN).

rows.statement: People can fall off at any step: not capturing everything, not deciding next actions, not reviewing; then the system fails.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L307 ('people can fall off on any one of those').
rows.note: '系统都会失效' is the script's summary. Allen lists the consequences (don't trust the lists, lists create as much stress as they relieve, it gets out of date) but does not use 'fail'. Fine as paraphrase.

rows.statement: His claims, such as the brain handling only a few things at once, are his own assertions with no research cited.
rows.source_locator: R/execution-system/talks/ferriss.txt L98 ('That's new cognitive science data, by the way'); R/execution-system/posts/p01.txt L27 ('cognitive science has validated in spades'); R/execution-system/posts/2015_03_getting-things-done-updated-for-2015.txt L45 ('I have added new research from the field of cognition').
rows.note: True for the interviews and handouts read. But Allen says the 2015 edition adds cognition research, and that text was not read (the ledger confirms this). The blanket sentence should be limited to the materials read.

rows.statement: Whether the method works is something the available materials show only through Allen's own account.
rows.source_locator: V/palantir-20261006/allen-gtd-official-excerpt.txt L25-47 (praise page: Alsop, Goldsmith, Magee and others) and L103 (client testimonial).
rows.note: The materials include third-party praise blurbs and a client testimonial. They are promotional, not studies. Accurate would be 'no independent study or evaluation'.

rows.statement: Bcc'd-to-all email and widely circulated meeting reports make information open across the company.
rows.source_locator: R/overview/data/saraf.clean.txt L56-58 (section 'Transparency to a ridiculous degree').
rows.note: '满天飞' is hyperbole; the source says 'very wide distribution - often the entire company'.

rows.statement: The cost falls on everyone: too much comes in.
rows.source_locator: R/overview/data/saraf.clean.txt L57-58 ('you faced two options: drown in your email ...'; 'The best part about this is that you could keep a running pulse of everything').
rows.note: Saraf calls the visibility 'the best part' and lists the inbox flood as one of two options. 'Cost' is the narrator's framing, not labelled as the narrator's own reading, and the segment does not mark it as such.

rows.statement: Ted Mabrey, head of global commercial, wrote that an FDE is accountable for the customer's end results and acts like the CEO but with no authority.
rows.source_locator: R/overview/data/mabrey.clean.txt L28 ('You must hold yourself accountable to the end results of the customers business and try to act as if you are the CEO, but with zero authority'); title: R/overview/data/stratechery.clean.txt L1 and L33 ('Head of Global Commercial Ted Mabrey').
rows.note: Drops 'try to'. The title is from the 2023 Stratechery interview.

rows.statement: The narrator's reading: many commitments, few people to direct, so the only thing to rely on is your own system; labelled as inference.
rows.source_locator: Script itself ('我的读法是 ... 这是推论').
rows.note: Correctly labelled as the narrator's reading. Its inputs (zero authority, Mabrey; capture / decide / weekly review, Allen) are supported above.

rows.statement: Apart from Saraf, the narrator found nobody who says how Palantir used the book.
rows.source_locator: R/overview/data/qureshi.clean.txt L46 ('at the time when you joined they sent you a copy of Impro, The Looming Tower, Interviewing Users, and Getting Things Done'); V/palantir-20261006/qureshi-reflections-on-palantir.html.txt L161; scratchpad/review/im-script.txt im.b19 (the series counts Qureshi when saying who spoke about Impro).
rows.note: Qureshi also says how Palantir used the book (sent it to new hires), and the series itself rests on that. Only Saraf ties it to the BCC and email-load practice. The sentence should be limited to that connection.

rows.statement: Next episode: Ray Dalio's early PDF, on how he treats mistakes and disagreement.
rows.source_locator: R/overview/data/qureshi.clean.txt L46 ('early PDF version of what became Ray Dalio's Principles'); V/palantir-series-20261017/dalio-principles-bwater-2015-public.txt (139 hits for 'mistake', 30 for 'disagree'); scratchpad/review/pr-script.txt pr.i1.
rows.note: Topic pointer; the PDF is the 2011-copyright public version.
